lore_anchors.definition: Xianxia recipes that produce superior pills but often require rare or near-extinct ingredients; modern formulas sacrifice potency for practicality.
A low-commitment master-disciple status with minimal instruction and limited obligations; contrasted with a personal disciple who receives real resources.
A Foundation Establishment elixir that slightly increases cultivation speed; one of two formulas Han Li received from Lei Wanhe.
Another Foundation Establishment elixir Han Li obtained; its specific function aligns with steady cultivation enhancement.
A foundational secret art for strengthening divine sense and enabling advanced puppet control; discovered by Han Li in the looted jade slip.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Lei Wanhe feel guilty about the trade?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because he's exchanging ancient formulas with hard-to-find ingredients for extremely valuable spirit herbs, and his conscience makes him warn Han Li about the difficulty.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why are ancient formulas considered inferior to modern ones?
cultural_notes_faq.a: They are superior in theory (better pill quality) but inferior in practice because their ingredients are extremely rare; modern formulas use more common substitutes but produce weaker effects.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Han Li's reaction to the "Great Derivative Art" so dramatic?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because encountering a rare, powerful technique in an unexpected place is a classic xianxia windfall—and Han Li's spiritual sense has always been his hidden strength, making this a perfect match.
